title: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) — Mock 11
pattern: WCL Asst. Foreman (Electrical) CBT (100 Q · 100 marks · 120 min · no −ve)

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: As per MVTR 1966, refresher vocational training must be given to persons employed in mines at least once in:
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 8: refresher training at least once in every 5 years.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: As per the Mines Rescue Rules 1985, a rescue station shall be under the charge of a Superintendent assisted by at least:
options: 2 instructors and a rescue brigade of at least 18 rescue-trained persons
questions.solution: MRR 1985: a rescue station has a Superintendent, at least 2 instructors and a rescue brigade of at least 18 rescue-trained persons.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An energy meter disc rotates faster when:
questions.solution: Higher power → more driving torque → faster disc rotation.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The correct connection of a single-phase wattmeter has:
options: Current coil in series and potential coil in parallel
Current coil in series and potential coil in series
questions.solution: Current coil in series with load; potential coil in parallel with load.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The two-wattmeter method is used to measure power in:
questions.solution: Two-wattmeter method measures total three-phase power in 3-wire systems.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In a balanced three-phase system with unity PF, the two wattmeters read:
questions.solution: At unity PF, both wattmeters read equal positive values.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: At zero power factor (purely reactive load), in the two-wattmeter method:
options: Both readings are equal and opposite
questions.solution: At zero PF, one reads +W and other −W. Total real power = 0.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The voltmeter-ammeter method for resistance measurement gives accurate results when measuring:
questions.solution: For low R: short shunt. For high R: long shunt.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In the short shunt connection of voltmeter-ammeter method, the voltmeter measures:
questions.solution: Short shunt: voltmeter connected directly across the unknown resistance.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Kelvin's double bridge is used to measure:
questions.solution: Kelvin bridge eliminates lead and contact resistance errors.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Kelvin bridge eliminates errors caused by:
questions.solution: Kelvin bridge uses additional ratio arms to nullify lead resistance effect.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Wheatstone bridge is used to measure:
questions.solution: Wheatstone bridge measures medium resistances accurately.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A Wheatstone bridge is balanced when:
questions.solution: Bridge balance: P/Q = R/S where P, Q are ratio arms.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A megger is used to measure:
questions.solution: Megger applies high DC voltage to measure insulation resistance in megaohms.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: For electrical machinery and plant, the competent person for inspection under CMR 2017 shall be an engineer or electrician holding qualifications specified in:
options: CEA (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations, 2010
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 213(6): the competent person for electrical machinery holds qualifications as specified in the CEA Safety & Electric Supply Regulations, 2010.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: While measuring insulation resistance with a megger, the measured resistance includes:
options: Surface leakage and volume insulation resistance
questions.solution: Megger measures total insulation resistance including surface leakage.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A multimeter can measure:
questions.solution: Multimeter combines voltmeter, ammeter, and ohmmeter functions.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A clamp meter measures current by:
options: Clamping a current transformer jaw around the conductor
Breaking the circuit and inserting the meter
questions.solution: Clamp meter uses split CT core that clamps around the conductor.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The advantage of a clamp meter is:
options: Non-invasive current measurement without breaking circuit
questions.solution: Clamp meter allows current measurement without disconnecting conductor.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: CRO stands for:
questions.solution: CRO displays voltage waveforms on a CRT screen.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The horizontal deflection in a CRO is produced by:
questions.solution: Sawtooth sweep generator deflects beam horizontally at constant rate.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The vertical deflection in a CRO is produced by:
options: Signal to be measured applied to Y-plates
questions.solution: Input signal applied to vertical (Y) deflection plates.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A digital multimeter (DMM) typically uses which type of A/D converter?
questions.solution: Dual-slope ADC provides high accuracy and noise rejection for DMM.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The advantage of a digital multimeter over analog is:
options: Higher input impedance and direct digital readout
questions.solution: DMM has very high input impedance and gives precise digital readout.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A power analyzer measures:
options: Voltage, current, power factor, harmonics, and power
questions.solution: Power analyzers measure V, I, PF, power, energy, harmonics, and flicker.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The true RMS value of an AC quantity is the:
options: Square root of mean of squares of instantaneous values
questions.solution: True RMS = √(mean of v²). Handles non-sinusoidal waveforms.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A PMMC instrument with a series multiplier is used as a:
questions.solution: High resistance in series with PMMC extends voltage range.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A PMMC instrument with a shunt is used as a:
questions.solution: Low resistance (shunt) in parallel extends current range.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The shunt resistance of an ammeter should be:
questions.solution: Shunt resistance must be very low to minimize voltage drop.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The multiplier resistance of a voltmeter should be:
questions.solution: Multiplier resistance must be very high to minimize current drawn.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The sensitivity of a voltmeter is expressed in:
questions.solution: Sensitivity (Ω/V) = 1/full-scale deflection current.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An ideal voltmeter has:
questions.solution: Infinite resistance ensures zero current drawn from circuit.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An ideal ammeter has:
questions.solution: Zero resistance ensures no voltage drop across the ammeter.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A PMMC instrument can be converted to measure AC by adding a:
questions.solution: Rectifier-type instrument uses rectifier bridge with PMMC to measure AC.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Under CMR 2017, a thorough inspection of all machinery and plant in use is required at least once in every:
options: 7 days, recorded in a bound paged book
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 213(5): a competent person thoroughly inspects all machinery and plant at least once in 7 days, recording results in a bound paged book.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Induction type energy meters work on the principle of:
options: Interaction of alternating fluxes producing rotating field
questions.solution: Alternating fluxes produce rotating field inducing eddy currents in disc.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Creeping in an energy meter is:
questions.solution: Creeping is slow disc rotation at no load due to incomplete magnet symmetry.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: To prevent creeping, energy meters are provided with:
options: A small hole or anti-creep notch in the disc
questions.solution: Anti-creep holes prevent continuous rotation at no load.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An kWh meter disc constant of 600 rev/kWh means:
options: The disc rotates 600 times per kWh of energy consumed
questions.solution: Meter constant: disc makes 600 revolutions per kWh consumed.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: If a 600 rev/kWh meter disc rotates 30 times in 2 minutes, the load is:

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A CT of ratio 200/5 A with a secondary ammeter reading 3.5 A indicates a primary current of:
questions.solution: Primary current = (200/5) × 3.5 = 140 A.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A PT of ratio 11000/110 V with secondary voltage of 105 V indicates a primary voltage of:

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The burden on a CT is expressed in:
questions.solution: CT burden is total VA load on the secondary.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Instrument transformers provide isolation between:
options: Primary conductor and secondary metering/relay circuits
questions.solution: CTs and PTs isolate high-voltage primary from metering/protection circuits.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A potentiometer measures voltage by:
options: Comparison with a known voltage (null-balance method)
questions.solution: Potentiometer compares unknown EMF against calibrated voltage at null.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The main advantage of a potentiometer is:
options: No current drawn from source at null — true EMF measurement
questions.solution: At null balance, no current flows from source, measuring true EMF.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: In a gassy seam of the second or third degree, no person shall supervise or operate electrical machinery unless he:
options: Holds a gas-testing certificate and carries an approved flame safety lamp
questions.solution: CMR 2017 Reg 213(2): in 2nd/3rd-degree gassy seams, operators of electrical machinery (other than telephones/signals/lamps) hold a gas-testing certificate and carry an approved flame safety lamp.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The Lissajous pattern on a CRO is used to measure:
options: Frequency ratio and phase difference between two signals
questions.solution: Lissajous figures help determine frequency ratio and phase.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A VTVM (Vacuum Tube Voltmeter) has the advantage of:
options: Very high input impedance compared to PMMC voltmeter
questions.solution: VTVM uses vacuum tube amplifier for very high input impedance.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An FET-based voltmeter has input impedance of the order of:
questions.solution: FET input stages provide extremely high input impedance (10¹⁰–10¹² Ω).

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Peak value of a sine wave can be measured using:
questions.solution: CRO directly shows peak value.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The average value of a full-wave rectified sine wave is:
questions.solution: Average of full-wave rectified sine = 2V_m/π = 0.637 V_m.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Form factor of a sinusoidal waveform is defined as:
questions.solution: Form factor = RMS/Average = π/(2√2) = 1.11 for sinusoidal wave.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Crest factor (peak factor) of a sine wave is:
questions.solution: Crest factor = V_peak/V_rms = √2 = 1.414 for sinusoidal waveform.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: An oscilloscope probe (10:1) is used to:
options: Attenuate signal by 10× and increase input impedance
questions.solution: 10:1 probe attenuates signal 10× and increases input impedance to ~10 MΩ.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Bandwidth of a CRO refers to:
options: Frequency range over which the vertical amplifier maintains specified accuracy
questions.solution: Bandwidth is the frequency range where vertical sensitivity is within ±3 dB.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A sampling oscilloscope is used to measure:
questions.solution: Sampling oscilloscope reconstructs high-frequency repetitive waveforms.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The function of the time base in a CRO is to:
options: Provide horizontal sweep at known rate for time measurement
questions.solution: Time base produces sawtooth waveform for horizontal deflection.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A digital power meter typically uses which method for power calculation?
options: Simultaneous sampling of V and I with DSP computation
questions.solution: Digital power meters sample V and I simultaneously, computing power using DSP.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A multimeter in resistance mode measures resistance by:
options: Passing a known current and measuring voltage drop
questions.solution: Internal battery supplies known current; measured voltage drop gives R = V/I.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: When measuring resistance with a multimeter, the reading includes:
questions.solution: Multimeter measures total R including test lead resistance.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The CEA regulations for electrical safety in mines were framed under which act?
questions.solution: CEA Regulations 2017 are framed under the Electricity Act 2003.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: As per DGMS Circular 2/2010, strata and dump slope monitoring is mandatory for dumps exceeding ______ in height.
questions.solution: DGMS Circular 2/2010: monitoring (including slope stability radar / real-time monitoring) is made mandatory for dumps exceeding 60 m height.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A shot-firer who has not been employed in blasting duties for more than 6 months shall undergo:
options: Retraining in the handling of explosives before resuming such duties
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 13: retraining in handling of explosives is required after an absence from such duties exceeding 6 months.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The maximum flame path gap for Class I Group IIA gases in a flameproof enclosure is:
questions.solution: Flame path gaps are precisely specified: ~0.2 mm for typical flange joints.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A person re-employed after an absence exceeding one year from mining work must undergo refresher training within:
questions.solution: MVTR 1966, Rule 10: refresher training within 1 month of re-employment after absence over 1 year.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Intrinsic safety (Ex i) limits electrical energy to prevent ignition by:
options: Ensuring stored energy is below ignition threshold of gas
questions.solution: Ex i limits voltage, current, and stored energy below minimum ignition energy.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The minimum ignition energy of methane (CH₄) is approximately:
questions.solution: Methane minimum ignition energy is ~0.28 mJ.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: IS standards for mining electrical equipment in India are specified by:
questions.solution: BIS publishes IS standards for mining equipment safety requirements.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: The permit to work system in mines for electrical maintenance involves:
options: Written permit specifying scope, safety measures, and authorized personnel
questions.solution: PTW is a formal written system ensuring all safety measures are verified.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: DGMS (Tech.) (S&T) Circular No. 02 of 2010 deals with:
options: Design, control and monitoring of pit and dump slopes in opencast mines
questions.solution: DGMS (Tech.) (S&T) Circular No. 02 dated 06.07.2010 concerns design, control and monitoring of pit and dump slopes in opencast mines.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A rescue-trained person shall practise with breathing apparatus at least:
options: 8 times a year, of which 4 in mines
4 times a year, of which 2 in mines
questions.solution: MRR 1985: rescue-trained persons practise with breathing apparatus at least 8 times a year, including 4 practices in the mine.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: CPR for electric shock victim involves:
options: Chest compressions and rescue breathing (30:2 ratio)
questions.solution: Standard CPR: 30 compressions followed by 2 rescue breaths.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A rescue room is required at a mine where the number of persons employed belowground exceeds 100 and:
options: The mine produces less than 100 tonnes a day
There is no rescue station within 35 km
questions.solution: MRR 1985: a rescue room is required when more than 100 persons work belowground and no rescue station is within 35 km.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A CO₂ fire extinguisher is most suitable for:
options: Class B and Class C (electrical) fires
questions.solution: CO₂ extinguishers are ideal for electrical and flammable liquid fires.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: A DCP (Dry Chemical Powder) extinguisher is effective against:
options: Class A, B, and C fires
questions.solution: DCP works on Class A, B, and C fires by chemical inhibition.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Water should NOT be used on which type of fire?
questions.solution: Water on oil fires can spread fire and cause splashing.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Foam extinguishers are effective on:
options: Flammable liquid (Class B) fires by smothering
questions.solution: Foam forms blanket over liquid surface, cutting off oxygen.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Under the Mines Rescue Rules 1985, the breathing apparatus kept at a rescue station or rescue room shall:
options: Be of the same type and make
Be of different types for flexibility
questions.solution: MRR 1985, Rule 11(4): breathing apparatus at a rescue station/room must be of the same type and make for interchangeability.

questions.subject: Electrical Engineering
questions.stem: Coal dust explosion can be prevented by:
options: Applying stone dust (inertite) on surfaces and in galleries
questions.solution: Stone dusting mixed with coal dust makes it non-explosible.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.stem: By selling 12 articles, a person gains the selling price of 2 articles. What is the profit percentage?
questions.solution: SP of 12 - CP of 12 = SP of 2 → SP of 10 = CP of 12 → profit on 12 = SP of 2. Profit% = (SP of 2/CP of 12) × 100. Since SP of 10 = CP of 12, CP = (10/12)SP. Profit = SP - (10/12)SP = (2/12)SP = SP/6 per article. Profit% = (SP/6) / (10SP/12) × 100 = (SP/6) × (12/10SP) × 100 = 20%

questions.stem: If in a certain code, DELHI is written as 12345 and PATNA is written as 67891, then how is LALIT written?
